text: forge coverage reports which lines, statements, branches, and functions your tests actually executed. It's a useful number. It is not proof your contract is correct.
A summary report shows percentages per file. For CI or an external dashboard, generate an LCOV tracefile instead with report lcov and report-file.

Coverage answers exactly one question: did any test execute this line. It says nothing about whether that test asserted the right thing — a test with no assertions still counts as covering every line it runs.
Branch coverage at 100% doesn't mean every combination across a sequence was tested — that's invariant testing. Line coverage doesn't mean boundary values were exercised — that's fuzz testing.
Use coverage as a map of blind spots, not a target. That closes out rigorous testing — Chapter 2 moves to automating all of it in CI.
